p: Vaticanus says Nebuchadnezzar brought "him" (Jeconiah); other codices say "them", all the captives.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD) and Codex Marchalianus (Q, 500s AD), in Swete's notes; the KJV ("brought them unto Babylon")
readings.en: and brought them in to Babylon

why: The Plain follows Swete's base text. "Him" keeps the focus on King Jeconiah, named at the start of the verse; "them" is the easier reading, since a list of captives comes between, and so is more likely to be a scribe's smoothing.

a: against the people of Israel and Judah
p: Three codices add Daniel 9:12's next words: "bringing great disasters on us".

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.orig: καὶ ἐπὶ ἄνθρωπον Ἰσραὴλ καὶ Ἰούδα
readings.en: and against man of Israel and Judah
readings.plain: against the people of Israel and Judah

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A), Codex Marchalianus (Q) and the Grottaferrata palimpsest (Γ, 700s-800s AD), in Swete's notes
readings.orig: καὶ ἐπὶ ἄνθρωπον Ἰσραὴλ καὶ Ἰούδα τοῦ ἀγαγεῖν ἐφ᾽ ἡμᾶς κακὰ μεγάλα
readings.en: and against man of Israel and Judah, to bring great evils upon us
readings.plain: against the people of Israel and Judah, bringing great disasters on us

why: The longer text matches Daniel 9:12 ("bringing a great disaster on us"), and scribes who knew Daniel's prayer could easily fill in the familiar words. The shorter text of Vaticanus is less likely to be an expansion. The KJV follows the shorter text here.
b: This variant shows how closely copyists heard Baruch 1:15-2:19 as a version of Daniel's prayer (see the note at 1:15).

p: Alexandrinus adds "and the bones of our officials", as in Jeremiah 8:1.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; Codex Marchalianus (Q); the KJV

readings.orig: τὰ ὀστᾶ βασιλέων ἡμῶν καὶ τὰ ὀστᾶ τῶν ἀρχόντων ἡμῶν
readings.en: the bones of our kings and the bones of our officials
readings.plain: the bones of our kings and the bones of our officials

why: Jeremiah 8:1 lists the bones of the kings and of the officials, and a scribe could add the officials from it. Most witnesses lack them.

a: shrink to a few among the nations
p: Vaticanus says the crowd will turn "into a small" number; others say it will turn "far away". One letter differs.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the KJV ("a small number") and the Latin
readings.orig: ἀποστρέψει εἰς μικρὰν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν
readings.en: will turn into a small (number) among the nations
readings.plain: shrink to a few among the nations

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Marchalianus (Q), in Swete's notes
readings.orig: ἀποστρέψει εἰς μακρὰν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν
readings.en: will turn far away among the nations
readings.plain: be turned away far off among the nations

why: "Small" answers "great" in the same sentence and matches Moses' warning that only a handful would be left (Deuteronomy 28:62). The Greek words mikran and makran differ by one letter, an easy slip.

p: Two codices, and the KJV, add "for you are a merciful God, and have mercy".

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
Codex Alexandrinus (A) and the margin of Codex Marchalianus (Q), in Swete's notes; the KJV ("for thou art merciful: and have pity upon us")
readings.orig: ἄκουσον, Κύριε, καὶ ἐλέησον, ὅτι θεὸς ἐλεήμων εἶ, καὶ ἐλέησον
readings.en: Hear, Lord, and have mercy, for you are a merciful God, and have mercy
readings.plain: Listen, Lord, and have mercy, for you are a merciful God, and have mercy,

why: The added words repeat "have mercy" and look like a reader's expansion from the common confession that God is merciful (Exodus 34:6). The shorter text is followed.

a: we have turned out of our hearts all the wrongdoing
t: Turned out of our hearts, or taken to heart?
p: Vaticanus' first hand says they turned the ancestors' sin "away from" their hearts; its correctors say "to" their hearts.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus, first hand (B*), as printed by Swete
readings.orig: ἀπεστρέψαμεν ἀπὸ καρδίας ἡμῶν πᾶσαν ἀδικίαν
readings.en: we turned away from our heart all wrongdoing
readings.plain: we have turned out of our hearts all the wrongdoing

readings.w: Correctors of Codex Vaticanus (Bab), Codex Alexandrinus (A) and Codex Marchalianus (Q), in Swete's notes; the KJV ("we have called to mind")
readings.orig: ἀπεστρέψαμεν ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἡμῶν πᾶσαν ἀδικίαν
readings.en: we turned to our heart (took to heart) all wrongdoing
readings.plain: we have taken to heart all the wrongdoing

why: Swete prints the first hand of Vaticanus, and the Plain follows his text. The other reading uses the idiom of 2:30 ("they will turn to their heart"), so it may be a correction toward that verse; or it may be original, and the first hand a slip. Both readings make sense: the exiles either have put away their ancestors' sins or have come to grips with them. The Latin, behind the Douay, reads "we are converted from the iniquity of our fathers".

t: The Everlasting, or the Holy One?
p: Alexandrinus reads "the glory of the Holy One".

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; Codex Marchalianus (Q); the KJV ("the glory of the Everlasting")
readings.en: of the glory of the Everlasting
of the glory of the Holy One
readings.plain: the glory of the Holy One

why: Both are titles of God in these chapters (4:10; 4:22). "The Everlasting" has the wider support.

t: A royal throne, or royal children?
p: Vaticanus pictures the returning exiles carried like a royal throne; other codices, the Latin and the KJV say "like royal children".

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
Codex Alexandrinus (A, which also lacks "as") and Codex Marchalianus (Q), in Swete's notes; the Latin (sicut filios regni); the KJV ("as children of the kingdom")

why: The Plain follows Swete's base text. "Throne" is the harder reading: the exiles are carried in procession as a king's throne is carried. "Sons of the kingdom" is easier and could come from a scribe thinking of the children of 5:5. The Latin and the KJV follow it.
